questions.q: How does CRM Analytics primarily differ from a native Salesforce report?
options: It queries the same objects live but with a different chart library
It can only be used on custom objects
It works on prepared datasets stored in the analytics platform rather than querying records live
It replaces the Salesforce database entirely
questions.explain: CRM Analytics extracts and prepares data into datasets that are stored and optimized for analysis, instead of querying object records live on each view.

questions.q: Which asset is the container that holds related dashboards and lenses and controls who can see them?
options: App
Dataset
Lens
Component
questions.explain: Apps are the unit of organization and sharing in CRM Analytics, similar in spirit to folders in native reports.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of this product's names, oldest to newest?
options: Tableau CRM, Wave Analytics, CRM Analytics, Einstein Analytics
Einstein Analytics, Wave Analytics, Tableau CRM, CRM Analytics
CRM Analytics, Tableau CRM, Einstein Analytics, Wave Analytics
Wave Analytics, Einstein Analytics, Tableau CRM, CRM Analytics
questions.explain: The product began as Wave, then Einstein Analytics, then Tableau CRM, and is now CRM Analytics. Older URLs still contain 'wave'.

questions.q: A dashboard user reports that CRM Analytics numbers lag a few hours behind Salesforce. What is the most likely reason?
options: The dataset behind the dashboard was last refreshed on a schedule and has not reloaded yet
The dashboard queries a cached copy of the browser history
CRM Analytics only updates once per month
Salesforce blocks live queries from Analytics Studio
questions.explain: Datasets are loaded on a schedule, so their data is only as fresh as the last refresh.

questions.q: In Analytics Studio, which page lets you filter all assets by type such as apps, lenses, and datasets?
options: Favorites
Browse
Watchlist
Notifications
questions.explain: Browse lists every asset and offers type filters such as All Items, Apps, Dashboards, Lenses, and Datasets.
